what_each_new_part_touches: Sub-step 1: four blue long pins go into the first 15-hole beam, with a black connector at its far end. Sub-step 2: a black hub with a blue pin goes onto the beam (yellow box).

Sub-step 3: the blue pump stands on three of the pins by its 1 x 3 base and the short blue hose is pushed onto its side nozzle (yellow box). Sub-step 4: the second 15-hole beam is pressed on under the pin ends. Page 20: the finished deck is placed on the turntable and the four blue pins of step 17 are pushed in from the sides (green arrows, two per side) to lock it.
where_everything_is_after: the pump deck (two 15-hole beams with the blue pump standing on it) sits on the turntable top and is held by the four blue pins pushed in from the sides

why.problem_solved: Builds the air pump that will later power the arm's air cylinders.
why.why_these_parts: A pump with a plunger pushed by hand pushes air through hoses; the two beams make a light frame for it.
why.sets_up_for_later: Steps 19-21 build the side frames and cross beam around the pump on the turntable.

review_note: Part numbers are likely (pump = 26288, hose 5102c04 from the 1:1 length check). Long pins counted at 220-450 dpi: they sit in every second hole (4, 6, 8, 10) of both beams; the hub covers holes 4-6 and the pump foot holes 8-10. The four turntable pins on page 20 and the hub/connector holes are still estimates. The pump's own points aren't in the catalog, so no join to the pump is written. Red box on page 19: pushing the black top up and down must move it; confirmation check only.
